required.locus: The Prophet ﷺ said: being rich is not about having lots of things.
required.note: A paraphrase placed directly after 'said:' with no closing boundary. The three sentences that follow sit inside the same construction, so a child hears all of it as his words. Not fabrication — attribution leaking.

required.locus: The richness is already inside you.
required.note: Contradicts the moral's own exercise: if the child already has it, there is nothing to do. Also misstates the matn — contentment of the nafs is cultivated, not possessed.

required.locus: Today, look at three things you own and say: I am thankful for this.
required.note: Gratitude with no object — thankful to whom. Also points the child back at possessions, the anchor the matn denies.

optional.locus: Notice how that feels inside your chest. That feeling is real richness.
optional.note: Qana'ah is a settled disposition, not a momentary sensation. Credited if flagged; overlaps with allah_absent_from_moral.

must_not_flag.locus: «Richness is not having many possessions, but richness is contentment of the soul.»
must_not_flag.note: Matches text_english verbatim. Flagging this as drift is a false positive.

must_not_flag.locus: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Ar-Riqaq (Softening of Hearts), number 6446, narrated by Abu Hurairah
must_not_flag.note: Attribution is correct. 6446 is Kitab ar-Riqaq; Abu Hurairah is the narrator.
